findings.summary: assertGlobDialect hard-codes the source label "afk.config.json", so a rejection raised through matchesGlob attributes the bad glob to the config file even when the caller supplied it from somewhere else.
findings.evidence: src/gate-policy.ts:212 calls assertGlobDialect(glob, CONFIG_FILENAME); matchesGlob("src/[ab].ts", "src/a.ts") throws "afk.config.json testGlobs glob \"src/[ab].ts\" contains the metacharacter \"[\"...\"" even though no afk.config.json was read and no testGlobs member was involved.
findings.expected: B-11 requires one shared validator so both entry points refuse identically and name what they rejected; it does not require the message to assert a provenance the matcher cannot know.
findings.observed: Every matchesGlob rejection claims the glob came from afk.config.json's testGlobs. #193 and #195 will be the first consumers to call matchesGlob with globs from a waiver or a CLI argument, and those users will be sent to the wrong file to fix it.
findings.clearCondition: matchesGlob either accepts an optional source/field label (defaulting to today's value, so parseGatePolicy and the default call still produce byte-identical messages and B-11 keeps passing) or its message drops the file/field attribution while still naming the offending character or segment.
